title: LP Building Solutions Turns 54: Celebrating More Than Five Decades of Innovation
summary: Celebrate LP Building Solutions’ 54th birthday by exploring the company’s journey from a pioneering forest products manufacturer to a leading innovator in engineered wood siding, structural solutions, sustainability, and homebuilding excellence.
body_text: On July 20, 2026, LP Building Solutions celebrates its 54th birthday—a milestone that reflects more than five decades of innovation, resilience, and leadership in the building products industry. Since our incorporation on July 20, 1972, LP has continually evolved to meet the changing needs of builders, remodelers, contractors, and homeowners while helping shape the future of home construction. Today, LP is recognized as a leading manufacturer of high-performance building products, offering solutions that help create homes that are beautiful, durable, and efficient. As the company marks 54 years of business, it’s worth looking back at the milestones that transformed LP from a young forest products company to an industry leader. The Beginning of LP LP was founded on July 20, 1972 and began trading on the New York Stock Exchange the following year. During this was a time of significant change in the building materials industry, and LP had a vision to develop innovative products that could improve how home and structures were built. Over the years, LP expanded its footprint across North and South America and relocated its headquarters to Nashville, Tennessee. Today, LP operates manufacturing facilities across multiple countries, serving customers throughout the construction industry. A Pioneer in Oriented Strand Board (OSB) One of LP’s earliest and most significant accomplishments came in 1979 when we began construction on North America’s first OSB mill in Hayward, Wisconsin. LP helped introduce a more scalable and efficient alternative during a time when plywood was dominating the market.OSB went on to become one of the most important wood products in modern construction. Its consistent performance and ability to utilize smaller, fast-growing trees helped revolutionize structural panel manufacturing. Today, OSB is widely used throughout residential construction and represents a major chapter in LP’s history of innovation. Hayward, Wisconsin mill Introducing LP® SmartSide® Trim & Siding Another defining moment took place in 1997 with the launch of LP® SmartSide® Trim & Siding. Building on decades of engineered wood expertise, LP developed a proprietary manufacturing process designed to enhance durability, resistance to moisture, termites, and fungal decay for long term strength in many weather conditions, all while preserving the natural beauty of wood. Over the past three decades, LP® SmartSide® Trim & Siding has become one of the fastest growing siding brands in the United States. Builders and homeowners have embraced the product for its combination of curb appeal, durability, and long-term performance. The portfolio continues to expand, including newer offerings such as LP® SmartSide® ExpertFinish® Trim & Siding and the LP® SmartSide® ExpertFinish® Trim & Siding Naturals Collection™ portfolio, a curated palette of prefinished siding colors. Building a Comprehensive Portfolio of Solutions While many know LP for siding, our impact extends across the entire building envelope. LP has developed a diverse range of structural and exterior products designed to help builders construct strong homes, efficiently. These include: LP WeatherLogic® Air & Water Barrier LP Legacy® Premium Sub-Flooring LP® TopNotch® 350 Durable Sub-Flooring LP® TechShield® Radiant Barrier Sheathing LP® FlameBlock® Fire-Rated Sheathing LP BurnGuard™ FRT OSB LP® Outdoor Building Solutions® LP® SmartSide® Trim & Siding LP® SmartSide® ExpertFinish® Trim & Siding LP® SmartSide® ExpertFinish® Trim & Siding Naturals Collection™ portfolio Together, these products demonstrate LP’s commitment to solving real-world construction challenges through innovation and performance. Advancing Sustainability in Construction As the industry increasingly focuses on environmental responsibility, LP has long invested in resource-efficient manufacturing and responsible forestry practices. Sustainability is a core part of LP's operations from environmental stewardship to responsible manufacturing operations. In 2025, 93% of our North American net sales were generated by carbon-negative products. Made primarily from renewable resources, these products provide builders with durable, high-quality alternatives to more energy-intensive, nonrenewable materials. As documented in our nine environmental product declarations, the associated LP® products store more carbon than they emit over their entire life cycles, helping to reduce emissions associated with the construction process. Continuing the Legacy of Innovation Innovation remains at the heart of LP. In recent years, we have continued to introduce new technologies and products designed to address emerging challenges in the industry. One example is LP BurnGuard™ FRT OSB, the first commercialized fire-retardant-treated OSB panel certified to meet applicable building codes for fire-retardant wood structural panels. Looking Ahead to the Future As LP Building Solutions celebrates its 54th anniversary, we are building on a strong foundation of innovation, quality, and customer focus. From pioneering OSB production to creating one of the industry's leading engineered wood siding brands, LP has consistently pushed the boundaries of what’s possible in construction. The challenges facing housing today, from affordability and housing inventory shortages to sustainability and resilience, create new opportunities for LP to innovate. With more than five decades of experience and a commitment to developing high-performance building solutions, LP is well-positioned to help shape the next generation of homes and communities. What began as a bold vision has grown into a company recognized for innovation, reliability, and leadership throughout the building industry. As LP celebrates this milestone anniversary, we also celebrate the team members, customers, partners, and communities that have helped make the journey possible. For more information on LP Building Solutions, visit our company overview!

title: FMC Corporation and Corteva Expand Access to Breakthrough Rimisoxafen Herbicide Technology
summary: FMC Corporation (NYSE: FMC) and Corteva, Inc. (NYSE: CTVA), two leading global agricultural science and innovation companies, today announced a co-exclusive strategic supply and license agreement that will expand access to FMC’s rimisoxafen technology across North and South America corn and soybean markets, adding an important new tool to each company’s respective herbicide portfolio.
body_text: FMC Corporation (NYSE: FMC) and Corteva, Inc. (NYSE: CTVA), two leading global agricultural science and innovation companies, today announced a co-exclusive strategic supply and license agreement that will expand access to FMC’s rimisoxafen technology across North and South America corn and soybean markets, adding an important new tool to each company’s respective herbicide portfolio. This collaboration will enable more growers across the Americas to control herbicide-resistant weeds, including Amaranthus species – the number one weed resistance challenge globally in soybeans and critical in cross-crop pressure in corn – with this groundbreaking dual mode of action herbicide technology. "This agreement ensures that more growers across the Americas will have access to rimisoxafen, one of the most innovative herbicide technologies developed in decades," said Leonardo Bastos, FMC vice president and chief marketing officer. "By working with Corteva, we are expanding the reach of this breakthrough technology to help growers effectively manage resistant weeds that threaten their productivity and profitability. Together, we are bringing growers a solution they urgently need. At the same time, FMC is committed to unlocking the full global potential of rimisoxafen across additional crops and geographies, reflecting our confidence in this molecule as a cornerstone of our innovation pipeline." Under the terms of the agreement, which extends through the next decade, FMC retains all rights of ownership to rimisoxafen and will supply Corteva with the active ingredient. Both companies will develop and commercialize their own exclusive premix formulations for the corn and soybean markets across North and South America, while FMC will continue to develop additional rimisoxafen-based products for other crops and geographies globally. Corteva will make an initial prepurchase payment of $200 million USD for product to be supplied by FMC. Together, both companies are committed to ensuring broad availability of this innovative technology and rapid adoption, supporting growers with durable weed management solutions for years to come. "By collaborating with FMC on rimisoxafen, we are expanding our ability to provide growers with advanced weed control tools that complement our portfolio," said Cynthia Ericson, Corteva vice president, weed control segment. "This agreement supports our long-term strategy of forging new collaborations that drive value for farmers, as well as a unique growth opportunity with attractive economics for Corteva above our current deep crop protection pipeline set to launch over the next decade." Rimisoxafen's dual mode of action creates a significantly higher barrier to resistance development compared to single mode of action herbicides, providing growers with an essential tool for managing weeds like palmer amaranth and waterhemp that have become resistant to multiple herbicide classes and cost farmers billions of dollars annually in lost yield. First commercial sales are anticipated by the end of the decade, pending applicable regulatory approvals. The Herbicide Resistance Action Committee recently classified rimisoxafen as the industry's first dual mode of action herbicide, recognizing its unique ability to control troublesome broadleaf weeds that threaten crop yields and farm profitability. Additional terms of the agreement were not disclosed. About FMC FMC Corporation is a global agricultural sciences company dedicated to helping growers produce food, feed, fiber and fuel for an expanding world population while adapting to a changing environment. FMC’s innovative crop protection solutions – including biologicals, crop nutrition, digital and precision agriculture – enable growers and crop advisers to address their toughest challenges economically while protecting the environment. FMC is committed to discovering new herbicide, insecticide and fungicide active ingredients, product formulations and pioneering technologies that are consistently better for the planet. Visit fmc.com to learn more and follow us on LinkedIn ®. About Corteva Corteva, Inc. (NYSE: CTVA) is a global pure-play agriculture company that combines industry-leading innovation, high-touch customer engagement and operational execution to profitably deliver solutions for the world’s most pressing agriculture challenges. Corteva generates advantaged market preference through its unique distribution strategy, together with its balanced and globally diverse mix of seed, crop protection, and digital products and services. With some of the most recognized brands in agriculture and a technology pipeline well positioned to drive growth, the Company is committed to maximizing productivity for farmers, while working with stakeholders throughout the food system as it fulfills its promise to enrich the lives of those who produce and those who consume, ensuring progress for generations to come. More information can be found at www.corteva.com . Always read and follow all label directions, restrictions and precautions for use. title: The cost-of-living crisis has accelerated the move to second hand
body_text: Energy bills are at an all-time high. Mortgage rates are at the highest level for 14 years. Last week the cost of a weekly shop rose at its fastest rate since 1980. While we all wait for the outcome of the Government’s budget in November, there’s only one question on retailers and shoppers' lips: when will prices stop rising? As inflation keeps creeping up, it’s fundamentally altering what consumers buy and how they shop. Our latest research found that three quarters (72%) of shoppers plan to cut-back on non-essential spending this year as the rising cost-of-living sets in. But, heading into a recession doesn’t always mean spending disappears. More often than not, spending just changes shape. Our new spending report, based on the spending insight of one in four UK bank accounts, found that increasing numbers of shoppers are turning to second hand marketplaces in response to the cost-of-living squeeze, swapping new for second hand in a bid to bag a bargain. Platforms like eBay, Depop and Vinted saw a 7% uptick in spend in the first half of the year, compared with the same period in 20211, while the average number of transactions made on these platforms rose 6%. Strikingly, this growth isn’t just coming from an increase in the number of people buying second hand – the average spend per person has also skyrocketed by 482% in the past three years, from £35.67 in 2019 to £207.63. No longer just a budget option, second hand fashion is increasingly the go-to for buying clothes. There’s no arguing that the cost-of-living crisis is accelerating a trend towards second hand shopping in search of better value. But the shift to second hand was already on the rise as the impact of the fashion industry on the planet was made all too evident. Almost half (47%) of shoppers say they plan to shop less at fast-fashion brands this year, and we’re seeing this play out across our spend data; spend on online fast fashion brands was down 4% year on year in the first six months of 2022, while the number of transactions fell by 16%. The cost-of-living crisis will undoubtedly make it more challenging for fashion retailers, as the competition for people’s dwindling disposable income gets tighter. Brands will need to work harder to keep and grow their customer spending and their market share. Harnessing the shift towards sustainability provides an opportunity to do this. While focusing on sustainability as a retailer has a positive impact on the planet and brand reputation, it increasingly also comes with benefits to a business’s bottom line. We’re already seeing some retailers take steps to introduce second hand or upcycled ranges, or even their own resale platforms, such as Zara’s newly launched pre-owned service or Urban Outfitters’ ‘Urban Renewal’ upcycled range. Even high street heavyweights like John Lewis are trialling their own fashion rental service. Rewards programmes that encourage second hand purchases or recycling clothing are another way to capitalise – for example offering discounts on end of line goods, or vouchers or cashback for bringing in clothes to be recycled can help drive further spending. Done right, these moves can not only improve brand perceptions, but turn into lucrative revenue streams. The cost-of-living crisis and tighter budgets have converged with a desire to reduce overconsumption and shop more consciously and the trend is showing no signs of slowing. Fashion brands that act now to capitalise on consumer concerns for their purse strings and the planet will reap the rewards in the long run. Download the UK State of Spend report here .

title: Adding Persistent Memory to Claude with Mem0
summary: We tested the Mem0 Claude connector with a real two-chat memory test: state a preference once, then see if Claude recalls it with zero hints. Here's what happened.
body_text: Quick Takeaways Find Mem0 in the Connectors Directory, and click Connect. It takes 2 minutes with no terminal and no config file required! A preference stated once gets retrieved unprompted in a completely separate chat, with zero shared vocabulary between the two prompts. Recall isn't guaranteed on every query. Claude decides, per turn, under Auto tool access , whether a memory lookup is worth making. ⚡ Try this yourself. Connect Mem0 from Claude's Connectors Directory and run the same two-chat test below. Claude is Anthropic's AI assistant, used for coding, research, writing, and everyday conversation. On its own, each chat starts fresh. Nothing carries over from one conversation to the next unless you're relying on Claude's own built-in memory inside claude.ai , which is scoped to that one product. On the other hand, Mem0 is a persistent memory layer for AI agents and assistants. It extracts facts from a conversation, stores them, retrieves the relevant ones later, and updates or deletes them as things change. It isn't tied to just one app: the same memory is reachable from Claude, Cursor, or any other MCP-compatible client. The Mem0 Claude connector is now listed in Anthropic's Connectors Directory, which links the two. Claude gets a memory store it can read from and write to mid-conversation, and Mem0's memory becomes usable directly inside a normal chat, no SDK required. Fig: Mem0 Claude connector listed in Anthropic's Connectors Directory A connector claiming persistent memory is easy to pitch and hard to verify from the outside. So, we did a two-chat test of the Mem0 Claude connector, where you mention a preference once in one chat. Open a new chat. Ask something adjacent, but never repeat the preference, and see whether Claude applies it anyway. Test at a glance Please enter a valid YouTube, Vimeo, or direct video URL Setup: Connecting Claude and Mem0 The connector needs to be authorized once before running the actual test, entirely inside Claude and one browser tab, no terminal, no config file. Here's that setup, step by step: Step 1: Click the + icon next to the message box, select Add connector . Step 2: Find Mem0 in the Directory and open it. Step 3: Click Connect , then authorize in the browser tab that opens. Step 4 : Sign in to the Mem0 platform using your email or GitHub account, pick an organization/ project, and click Connect to Mem0 . Mem0 generates an API key automatically; nothing to copy or paste. Claude chat window confirms Connected to Mem0. Step 5: Run a sanity check within a new Claude chat. Once Claude confirms the connector is available, you're ready to test it. Chat 1: Stating a preference naturally Let's plan a 4-day San Francisco trip with Claude and add some details about your preferences and the places you want to visit. Note: When Claude asks permission before writing, "Claude wants to use Add memory from Mem0", Click Always allow . Now, let's iterate and swap in a Napa day trip. Then, mid-conversation, mention that "I'm a vegetarian, keep that in mind for wherever we eat." Note: With Mem0 active in this chat, Claude saves the fact that you're vegetarian. The preference was mentioned once, never repeated, never flagged with "remember this.” Chat 2: Testing recall with zero hints Now for the real test: open a new chat and see whether Claude actually remembers what we told it, without any hints this time. Claude tags the response "Tailored vegetarian recommendations" and opens with: "SF has a great food scene for a vegetarian who wants a relaxed pace with a couple of splurges." Every pick that follows is vegetarian-aware, split into casual lunches and splurge-worthy dinners, matching preferences stated in a completely different conversation. Run it yourself 01 Connect Mem0 from the Connectors Directory (steps above) 02 Confirm access explicitly before testing anything: "Do you have access to Mem0?" 03 State one specific, checkable preference in passing, during a real conversation, without flagging it. 04 Open a new chat and ask something adjacent that shares zero vocabulary with the original preference Further Reading The 2026 Token Optimization Playbook Cut AI Agent Memory Costs State Of AI Agent Memory 2026 Give Your AI Agent Memory And Guardrails Mem0 Docker Sandboxes Memory Poisoning: How Bad Inputs Corrupt Your AI Agent's Memory

title: Ariel is Good!
summary: Meet tattoo artist and owner of East Coast Social Club, Ariel, as she discusses what drew her to tattooing and why she turned to Venue.
body_text: What do you get when you combine a love of UFC, Fast & Furious movies, and hip hop culture with cutie-pie Sanrio, Kewpies, and anime characters? You get an Arielisgood tattoo. After Ariel graduated from business school, she became infatuated with tattooing and realized there was a hole in the industry that she wanted to fill. Tattooing, like any art form, can feel a bit elitist and exclusionary to those just starting to dip their toes in and Ariel sought to make tattoos feel more accessible to clients looking for delicate ways to decorate their vessel. After an apprenticeship and residencies at several different shops across NYC, Ariel used her business degree to open East Coast Social Club, located in East Williamsburg. Now she gets to be the boss and over the last two and a half years has created a dreamy artist’s playground complete with salon chairs upstairs, a podcasting studio in the basement, and a backyard, perfect for a summer kickback. The space reflects her personality and tattoo aesthetics beyond measure–bright, clean, colorful and adorable. But it’s not all cutesy! Ariel loves art in all forms and wants to create tattoos that subvert expectations, think Hello Kitty with a face tat or a Kewpie baby decked out in barbed wire and skulls.

title: Ryde Appoints Chief Product Officer to Accelerate Platform Innovation and Marketplace Growth
body_text: SINGAPORE, SG / ACCESS Newswire / May 18, 2026 / Ryde Group Ltd (NYSE: RYDE ) ("Ryde" or the "Company") a leading technology platform for mobility and quick commerce in Singapore, today announced the appointment of James Tan as Chief Product Officer ("CPO") . In this role, James will lead Ryde's end-to-end product strategy, platform optimisation, and product-led growth initiatives as the Company accelerates its next phase of development. A Proven Product Leader with Deep Platform Knowledge James brings over 12 years of experience in product management, design, and digital platform development, including more than 8 years at Ryde where he has been central to the Company's platform evolution. During his tenure, James has led cross-functional teams spanning engineering, operations, customer experience, marketing, and business development, consistently delivering measurable improvements in marketplace performance and user experience. Prior to his appointment as CPO, James earned his stripes as a core member of the team that built and scaled Ryde into Singapore's first ride-hailing company to list on the NYSE American - a milestone that reflects both the platform's maturity and the calibre of the team behind it. His track record includes driving over 70% growth in Ryde+ subscriptions within three months - one of the strongest subscription growth periods in the platform's history - through targeted improvements in user engagement, subscription optimisation, and platform experience. Strategic Product Priorities for the Next 12 Months Under James's leadership, Ryde will execute a focused set of product initiatives targeting measurable gains in marketplace efficiency, driver retention, and rider experience: Smarter driver job allocation - Automated job matching to reduce average rider wait times, with phased rollout targeted from Q4 2026 Enhanced marketplace matching - Machine learning-driven optimisation to improve successful ride match rates and reduce booking friction Driver operational tools - Improved earnings visibility and platform tools to strengthen driver engagement and supply stability Rider personalisation and loyalty - Targeted features to improve long-term retention and Ryde+ subscription adoption Platform analytics and intelligence - Expanded data capabilities to support operational decision-making and scalable growth Ryde targets measurable improvement across ride match rates, average rider wait times, and platform engagement within 12 months, underpinned by these initiatives. Leadership Commentary "As Ryde continues to scale, product innovation and operational efficiency remain central to our long-term growth strategy," said Terence Zou, Founder, Chairman and CEO of Ryde . "James brings the product depth, operational understanding, and execution track record we need as we strengthen the platform for both drivers and riders. His appointment reflects our commitment to building a smarter, more efficient, and more accessible mobility ecosystem." "Product innovation is not about releasing features - it is about solving real operational challenges at scale," said James Tan, Chief Product Officer of Ryde. "Our focus is on building a more intelligent and seamless platform that improves marketplace performance while delivering a meaningfully better experience for drivers and riders alike." A Differentiated Model Built for Sustainable Growth Unlike platform-centric competitors, Ryde operates on a driver-first, 0% commission model - a structural advantage that drives superior driver retention, supply stability, and long-term marketplace sustainability. James's appointment reinforces the Company's commitment to deepening this differentiation through continuous platform investment and operational excellence. About Ryde Group Ltd Ryde is a super mobility app founded in Singapore and recognised as the world's FIRST on-demand carpooling app since 2014. As a publicly listed company on the NYSE American, Ryde is reimagining the way people and goods move around by offering a full suite of services, including carpooling, private hire, taxi, and delivery. What distinguishes Ryde is its commitment to empowering private-hire and taxi partners by taking 0% commission, ensuring that drivers retain more of their hard-earned earnings. title: Beer Packaging Trends for Sustainability and More
summary: Beer Packaging Trends for Sustainability and More
body_text: The beer industry is entering a new era. Once defined largely by tradition and taste, the category is being reshaped by forces that reach far beyond the brewery. Changes in consumer behavior, sustainability expectations, and lifestyle choices are transforming not only what’s inside the bottle or can, but how it’s delivered, displayed and experienced. From global powerhouses to local craft labels, brewers are expanding portfolios, experimenting with flavors and refining production methods to align with evolving priorities around wellness, responsibility and environmental impact. At the same time, retailers and regulators are driving change in how beer reaches consumers, increasing pressure on brands to innovate through every part of the value chain — including packaging. In this new landscape, beer packaging is more than protection or presentation; it’s a strategy. The right format can help brewers reduce plastic, lower emissions and connect more authentically with modern drinkers. It’s a vital medium for differentiation and proof of purpose. As a trusted partner to both craft breweries and global brands, we see the evolution of the beer category as an opportunity to leverage beer packaging trends to deliver performance, sustainability and brand experience. Here are three powerful shifts redefining the future of beer — and shaping the next wave of beer packaging innovation and sustainable beer packaging around the world. 1. Responsible Brewing Calls for Sustainable Beer Packaging As expectations rise, sustainability is becoming a key driver of choice — shaping brewing methods, beer packaging design, consumer perception and more. Today’s beverage consumers gravitate toward brands that care about sustainability, giving brewers the chance to differentiate themselves and attract new customers through their commitment to the environment.1 Consumers around the world are willing to put their money where their values are. As reported in an online Food Engineering article, an international survey across seven countries found that almost half of the respondents would choose a more expensive but more sustainably produced beer over a less expensive and less sustainable option. Beer packaging — whether primary, secondary or tertiary — plays a critical role in reducing a brand’s environmental footprint and conveying its values.2 As evolving consumer preferences and tightening legislation such as EU packaging waste regulations accelerate the transition away from single-use plastics, manufacturers are increasingly turning to alternative, sustainable beer packaging materials like paper to meet performance needs while supporting circularity goals.3 Paper-based multipack solutions like CanCollar® and PETCollar™ are helping brewers move out of plastic rings and shrink wrap, replacing them with recyclable, paper-based carriers that deliver strong handling performance, smooth line integration and standout shelf presence. Ultimately, more sustainable beer manufacturing and beer packaging design is a win-win for all. Consumers feel good about their purchasing choice; beer brands differentiate themselves from competitors; and with 190 billion liters of beer brewed in 2024,4 the potential for a positive environmental impact is profound. Packaging takeaway: Recyclable, paper-based can packaging and bottle packaging can help your brand reduce its environmental footprint while aligning with consumers’ values and helping your product stand out. 2. Mindful Drinking is Crafting the Future of Beer Packaging Innovation Health and wellness are reshaping how consumers drink, inspiring lighter, low-alcohol options and packaging innovations that reflect moderation, balance and purpose. Driven by a focus on health and wellness, more consumers are seeking alternatives to traditional beer that allow them to embrace health goals without sacrificing the social experience. “Beer lovers across the country are turning to low- and no-alcohol beers as their go-to choice to meet moderation goals,” said Brian Crawford, president and CEO of the Beer Institute.5 The result? The global market for non-alcoholic beer has at least tripled in the last five years.6 “Non-alc beer is the fastest growing segment in the beer industry, consistently growing by double digits over the past few years,” said Andrew Heritage, chief economist at the Beer Institute.7 As the no- and low-alcohol category continues to expand, packaging formats play an increasingly important role in signaling moderation. For instance, slim cans have become a popular choice for portion control and are often associated with lower-calorie, lighter options. This movement toward healthier cues also influences how breweries think about packaging operations. Modern packaging lines can typically accommodate slim-can formats without requiring an entirely new machine — only new tooling — giving brands the agility to introduce alternative sizes that support mindful-drinking trends without major capital investment. Packaging takeaway: For beer brands looking to capitalize on the low- and no-alcohol trend, thoughtful, premium packaging design can convey your product’s message of health and wellness, while future-proof beverage packaging automation can help you seamlessly adapt to changing consumer preferences. 3. As Flavor Evolves, Beer Packaging Design Levels Up Today's beer drinkers are embracing bold new flavors, pushing beer packaging design to capture creativity, color and storytelling that match their adventurous taste preferences. From international flavors to surprising ingredients, Tastewise’s article , “Craft Beer Trends: The Coolest Brews of 2025” highlights that beer brands are pushing boundaries to stay a step ahead in the market and embrace consumers’ desire for new and exotic tastes. As brewers responded to the growing popularity of flavored variants in other alcoholic segments,8 global flavored beers launches have grown 7% over the past five years. Fruit flavors have proven to be the most popular, but other emerging flavor categories include spices, cake, cookies, pie, vegetables and desserts.9 Packaging Takeaway: Innovative flavors need packaging that reflects and promotes the uniqueness of your beer. Bold visuals, unique silhouettes and vibrant storytelling can help communicate novelty and stand out on crowded shelves. For brewers, packaging is no longer simply the protective layer around the product — it’s a direct expression of what the brand stands for. It signals values. It influences shopper decisions. It reflects quality, care and purpose. We partner with beer brands of every size to bring these opportunities to life. From automated paper-based multipack systems that eliminate plastic, to premium formats that elevate shelf appeal and strengthen differentiation, we design solutions that meet performance requirements today while aligning with where the category is headed next. If you’d like to see how we can help you advance your sustainability goals with our innovative beer packaging , contact us today .

title: The 80/20 Rule of Energy: How to Focus on What Actually Matters
summary: The 80/20 Rule of Energy: How to Focus on What Actually Matters
body_text: Ever finish a workday feeling exhausted… but not actually accomplished? You answered the emails, sat in the meetings, crossed off some to-dos—and somehow, your most meaningful project didn’t budge. Your creative energy ? Scattered. Your focus? Spent on the wrong things. Here’s where the 80/20 rule comes in. Originally known as the Pareto Principle , this idea suggests that 80% of outcomes come from just 20% of efforts . And when applied to your energy, it changes everything. Because if you know where your real focus should go, you don’t have to do more—you just need to do what matters most . Let’s explore how to apply the 80/20 rule to your work, your focus, and your energy. Most of Your Impact Comes From a Few Key Actions It’s not about being lazy. It’s about being selective. Think about your week. Which tasks… Move the needle forward on your most important goals? Lead to the biggest results in your creative work or business? Light you up instead of draining you? Chances are, it’s a small handful of high-impact actions—writing, ideating, designing, problem-solving, or deep strategy. These are the 20% activities that bring in 80% of your results. Everything else? Admin. Busywork. Unnecessary meetings. Half-hearted multitasking . It’s not bad, but it might not deserve your best hours. When you identify your “vital few” energy tasks, you can start building your workweek around them , instead of reacting to everything equally. Energy, Not Just Time, Is the Real Currency The 80/20 rule is usually applied to productivity and time—but energy is a whole different game. You might have 8 hours blocked for work, but only 2 good hours of actual focus. The trick is to spend your best energy on your most meaningful work , and let the rest stretch or shrink accordingly. Ask yourself: What time of day do I feel most alert, creative, or focused? Which tasks drain me faster than they should? Am I accidentally giving my “prime focus” to low-impact tasks? By aligning your peak energy windows with your 20% activities , you start to see real momentum—without overextending yourself. How to Find Your 20% Energy Priorities Try this weekly reset practice: List everything you did last week. Seriously. Write it all down. Every email, task, call, or deliverable. Circle what actually created results. What led to progress, money, clarity, creativity, or connection? Notice the tasks that made you feel fulfilled or proud. These don’t always show up on spreadsheets—but they matter. Identify what drained your energy the most. Were they even necessary? Could you delegate, delay, or delete? Now you’ve got a personal map of what’s worth your energy—and what isn’t. Working Smarter, Not Softer When we talk about “gentle productivity,” we don’t mean avoiding hard things. We mean spending your energy like it’s valuable—because it is. Applying the 80/20 rule doesn’t mean you’ll never have to do boring admin again. But it does mean you’ll start protecting your energy from things that steal your focus without offering much in return. This might look like: Starting your day with your high-impact task before checking Slack. Blocking one afternoon a week for deep work (and guarding it fiercely). Using a sound cue—like a playlist or chime—to signal that it’s time for your 20%. Because small systems can lead to big clarity. Final Thought: You Don’t Need More Discipline—You Need a Better Filter You’re not behind. You’re just over-committed to the wrong 80%. Once you know what actually drives your energy, your fulfillment, and your forward momentum, you can start giving yourself permission to let the rest be lighter . More aligned. More focused. Less scattered. That’s the magic of the 80/20 rule—not just for productivity, but for peace. 🧠 Journal Prompt: What’s one task I can move to my “vital 20%” list—and how can I protect time for it this week? title: Omnichannel Commerce & B2B Digital Transformation with the Advanced Success Plan for SAP Customer Experience
summary: Omnichannel commerce and B2B digital transformation, with focus on CX and end-to-end service execution.
body_text: Modern B2B buyers expect seamless experiences across web, mobile, marketplaces, and partner portals. In fact, 84% of B2B buyers say it is important for suppliers to operate across multiple online and offline channels.* Turn transformation strategies into action through a coordinated set of services and guidance for every stage of your journey Learn how To meet these expectations, organizations must move beyond siloed commerce channels toward a connected autonomous CX model that integrates commerce, order sourcing, fulfilment, and customer support across the full customer journey. The Advanced Success Plan for SAP Customer Experience supports this shift by accelerating omnichannel capability build-out through outcome-based governance. It helps organizations move from fragmented execution to coordinated operations—enabling consistent cross-channel experiences, aligning commerce with sales and service execution, and improving conversion and repeat purchase through end-to-end alignment. Reality of B2B buying B2B buying is rarely linear anymore. Buyers often switch between digital channels, sales teams, and service touchpoints before deciding. Research from McKinsey’s B2B Pulse highlights that buyers typically engage across multiple interaction channels before making a decision.** This reflects how digital commerce has become a core part of the buying process, with 58% of global B2B retailers selling on at least three e-commerce platforms.† At the same time, expectations have shifted. Consistency across channels is assumed, digital self-service is often the starting point, and speed and transparency are baseline requirements. That creates a dual challenge for organizations: improving customer experience while also managing increasing operational complexity behind the scenes. Convergence of commerce, sales, and service B2B environments combine complex operations with tightly connected customer journeys. Organizations must manage customer-specific pricing and contracts, large and dynamic product catalogs, multi-step approvals, distributed fulfilment models, and integrations across commerce, ERP, sales, and service systems. Customers, however, do not see this complexity. They experience a single journey, from discovery to purchase, fulfilment, and support, and expect it to feel seamless. A typical journey may include discovering products online, aligning pricing with sales, placing orders through self-service channels, and resolving issues via service interactions. Expectations for real-time visibility, fast issue resolution, and consistent engagement continue to rise, as highlighted in research such as DHL’s B2B E-Commerce Trends. The same DHL report also shows that 78% of B2B retailers expect website sales to grow over the next three to five years, which reinforces how central digital channels have become.† Yet many organizations still operate in silos. The result is often inconsistent data, limited visibility across interactions, slower issue resolution, and disconnected customer experiences. This is why omnichannel transformation is not about adding channels, but about connecting commerce, sales, and service into a unified operating flow. Process excellence as a foundation As complexity increases, end-to-end process alignment becomes critical. Customers experience outcomes, not systems, and those outcomes depend on how well processes are connected across commerce, sales, service, and fulfilment. Breakdowns typically occur when sales agreements are not reflected in commerce systems, fulfilment is not aligned with order promises, service teams lack customer context, or data differs across channels. These are not isolated system issues, but symptoms of disconnected processes. In practice, that can mean a customer sees one price in the portal, a different one in the quote, and another one in the order confirmation. It can also mean service teams have to ask customers to repeat information that already exists elsewhere in the organization. Even when the underlying technology is in place, the experience still feels broken if the process is not connected. Organizations that invest in process excellence are better positioned to deliver consistent experiences, reduce friction, improve operational efficiency, and scale complex B2B models. Process alignment also makes it easier to respond to change, because teams can adapt faster when the underlying journey is not held together by disconnected handoffs. Why omnichannel matters Omnichannel in B2B is not just about offering more ways to buy. It is about making those ways work together. When the customer starts on one channel and finishes on another, the handoff needs to feel natural. If not, the customer experience becomes fragmented very quickly. That matters because B2B buyers are increasingly comparing their business purchasing experience to the consumer experiences they already know. They expect simple navigation, transparent pricing, reliable order updates, and a service team that understands the full context of the account. In other words, they want the convenience of digital commerce without losing the support and complexity that B2B purchasing often requires. This is also where many companies struggle. They may have a strong storefront, but weak back-end coordination. Or they may have good sales support, but poor visibility once the order has been placed. Omnichannel transformation closes that gap by connecting the customer-facing experience with the operational processes behind it. Accelerating outcomes with the Advanced Success Plan for SAP Customer Experience The Advanced Success Plan for SAP Customer Experience helps organizations accelerate omnichannel capability build-out through outcome-based governance and alignment between strategy and execution. Rather than focusing only on implementation, the emphasis is on measurable outcomes across the full customer journey. This includes enabling consistent omnichannel experiences, aligning SAP Commerce Cloud, SAP Sales and Service Cloud, and fulfilment processes, managing catalog and contract complexity at scale, improving order sourcing and fulfilment coordination, and strengthening end-to-end process alignment. The goal is to ensure all capabilities operate as one connected system rather than separate functions. That becomes especially important in B2B environments where a single transaction can involve multiple stakeholders, custom pricing rules, approval steps, and several systems working together at once. Without clear governance and alignment, even well-designed digital tools can create confusion instead of clarity. With the right operating model, however, organizations can turn complexity into a strength. They can reduce friction for customers, improve efficiency internally, and create a more reliable buying experience across every channel. The Advanced Success Plan for SAP Customer Experience includes access to Business Process Best Practices which helps customers understand the end-to-end process flow and best practices for executing business processes across SAP Sales and Service. This service showcases reference processes and bridges the gaps that can occur during rapid implementations of solutions in complex landscapes or when implementation of multiple solutions creates fragmented processes without taking into consideration unique end-to-end view. Conclusion Omnichannel commerce and B2B digital transformation are reshaping how organizations engage customers and deliver value. Success depends on connecting commerce, sales, service, and fulfilment into a unified operating model supported by strong end-to-end processes. Organizations that focus on process excellence and outcome-based governance are better positioned to scale effectively and meet rising customer expectations. The Advanced Success Plan for SAP Customer Experience enables this by connecting strategy to execution and supporting consistent outcomes across the customer journey. For B2B companies, the real shift is not just digital adoption. It is building a model where channels, processes, and teams work together in a way that feels simple to the customer, even when the operation behind it is complex. Nikola Stojanovski is a product manager for the Advanced Success Plan for SAP Customer Experience. Tara Tracey is global product owner for the Advanced Success Plan for SAP Customer Experience. title: Insurance conferences commercial brokers must attend in 2026: the fall circuit
summary: Verified dates, venues, and links for every insurance conference worth a commercial broker’s calendar from August through November 2026: ITC Vegas, the ABU regional mini-vention, CIAB’s Insurance Leadership Forum, WSIA, TMPAA, and more. CopyCat will be exhibiting at ITC Vegas and ABU.
body_text: The short version Eleven events between August 28 and November 11, with dates checked against each organizer’s own site in July 2026. ITC Vegas (Sept 29 to Oct 1, Mandalay Bay) is the technology show. CIAB, WSIA, and TMPAA are the meeting shows, where the value is a calendar booked weeks ahead. ABU’s national convention already passed. The next ABU event is the one-day Southern California Mini-vention on August 28 in Ontario, CA. CopyCat will have a booth at ABU and at ITC Vegas. November is quiet for commercial P&C. Only one national event lands, and it is life and annuity. The insurance conference calendar is front-loaded into fall. Between late August and mid-November 2026, a commercial broker can hit a one-day regional trade show, the largest insurtech gathering in the world, the meeting where the biggest brokerage CEOs negotiate carrier relationships, and the two events where wholesale and program business actually gets placed. You cannot go to all of them. Below is the fall circuit with verified dates, venues, and official links, organized by month, with a note on who each one is genuinely for. Always re-check the organizer page before booking travel, because venues and dates do move. Fall 2026 at a glance Event Dates Location Best for ABU SoCal Mini-vention Aug 28 Ontario, CA Regional agents, CE, markets IIABAZ Annual Convention Sep 2 to 3 Phoenix, AZ Southwest agencies American Agents Alliance Sep 24 to 26 Palm Desert, CA Western P&C, appointments Applied Net Sep 28 to Oct 1 National Harbor, MD Applied, EZLynx, Ivans users ITC Vegas Sep 29 to Oct 1 Las Vegas, NV Technology evaluation Big “I” Fall Leadership Sep 30 to Oct 3 Baltimore, MD Association leadership CIAB Insurance Leadership Forum Oct 2 to 6 Colorado Springs, CO Brokerage C-suite WSIA Annual Marketplace Oct 11 to 14 San Diego, CA Wholesale and E&S TMPAA Annual Summit Oct 19 to 21 Scottsdale, AZ Program business CPCU Society In2Risk Oct 19 to 21 Las Vegas, NV Technical education, CPCU Protectors Vegas Nov 9 to 11 Las Vegas, NV Life, annuity, benefits Dates and venues verified against organizer websites in July 2026. Confirm on the official event page before booking. August 2026 ABU Southern California Summertime Mini-vention August 28, DoubleTree by Hilton Ontario Airport, Ontario, CA. Agent Brokers United runs the best kind of regional event: one day, one room, low cost, and everyone in it actually writes business. The venue is at 222 N Vineyard Ave, and the day runs 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Time What happens 9:00 a.m. to noon Workers’ compensation continuing education class Noon to 1:00 p.m. Lunch 1:00 to 4:00 p.m. Trade show floor 5:00 p.m. After-party with food, drinks, and music Admission is $50 for agents and brokers, $150 for company representatives without table space, and $850 for an exhibitor table. For a Southern California agency, that is the cheapest CE credit plus carrier-appointment conversation you will find all year. ABU’s national trade show convention is a separate, larger event held every spring at Planet Hollywood in Las Vegas. The 2026 edition ran April 28 to 30, so the next one is April 28 to 30, 2027. Go if you are a California independent agency owner or producer who wants CE, market access, and a short drive. September 2026 IIABAZ 92nd Annual Convention & Trade Show September 2 to 3, JW Marriott Phoenix Desert Ridge Resort & Spa, Phoenix, AZ. Big “I” Arizona’s 92nd annual convention. The trade show on September 3 runs 2:00 to 6:30 p.m. with roughly 133 exhibit booths, and it is free to attend. Former Arizona Cardinal Jake Plummer keynotes the luncheon. Go if you write in the Southwest and want market face-time without a full week away. American Agents Alliance Conference & Expo September 24 to 26, JW Marriott Desert Springs Resort & Spa, Palm Desert, CA. The Alliance bills itself as the largest P&C insurance event in the West. It is built around carrier appointments, continuing education, an expo floor, a golf tournament, and the networking that comes with a three-day resort format. Go if you are a Western independent agency chasing new carrier appointments and markets. Applied Net 2026 September 28 to October 1, Gaylord National Resort & Convention Center, National Harbor, MD. Applied Systems and Applied Client Network bring the Applied, EZLynx, and Ivans user community together just outside Washington, DC. This is the agency-management-system event. If your operations run on Applied Epic or EZLynx, this is where the roadmap, the integrations, and the power users are. Go if you own agency operations, data, or the AMS itself. ITC Vegas 2026 (InsureTech Connect) September 29 to October 1, Mandalay Bay Convention Center, Las Vegas, NV. 9,000+ attendees, per the organizer 500+ speakers across the tracks 3 days Sept 29 to Oct 1 The big one, and the largest gathering of insurance leaders, innovators, and investors anywhere. Tracks cover growth, operational efficiency, strategic foresight, and life, benefits and annuities. Practical logistics from the organizer: sessions start as early as 8:30 a.m., the expo floor is open 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. on September 30 and 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. on October 1, and they recommend arriving Monday, September 28 and leaving Friday, October 2. A word of advice for brokers specifically. ITC is a technology show, not a market show. You will not leave with new carrier appointments. You will leave with a clear picture of what is actually shipping in AI for distribution, and which vendors can survive a real document instead of a scripted demo. Bring your ugliest carrier PDF and make people run it. Go if you are evaluating technology, buying it, or trying to figure out what your competitors will be running next year. Big “I” Fall Leadership Conference September 30 to October 3, Hilton Baltimore Inner Harbor, Baltimore, MD. The national Big “I” leadership meeting. The Education Convocation runs September 29 to October 1 and the Young Agents Leadership Institute runs October 1 to 3, both at the same hotel. Go if you are active in association leadership, state association governance, or young agents programs. October 2026 The Council’s Insurance Leadership Forum October 2 to 6, The Broadmoor, Colorado Springs, CO. ILF is the premier marketplace meeting for top-tier broker executives in commercial property and casualty. The Council reports more than 1,200 attendees, heavily weighted toward C-suite executives, practice leaders, and decision makers. This is a relationship and negotiation meeting rather than an education conference, and the calendar is wall-to-wall private carrier meetings. Go if you sit at the top of a brokerage and own carrier relationships. Otherwise this is not your event. WSIA Annual Marketplace October 11 to 14, Manchester Grand Hyatt San Diego and Marriott Marquis San Diego Marina, San Diego, CA. The Wholesale & Specialty Insurance Association’s Annual Marketplace is the premier networking and business event for the wholesale, specialty, and surplus lines industry. As with ILF, the value is in the pre-booked meeting schedule, not the sessions. Go if you place E&S business and want concentrated wholesale market time. Book meetings months ahead, because the calendar fills before you arrive. TMPAA 26th Annual Summit October 19 to 21, The Westin Kierland Resort & Spa, Scottsdale, AZ. The Target Markets Program Administrators Association Summit is where program business gets done. TMPAA expects more than 2,000 attendees across three groups: program administrators, carriers, and service providers. It grew from 150 attendees at the first Summit. Go if you run a program, want to launch one, or need carrier capacity for a niche book. CPCU Society In2Risk October 19 to 21, Las Vegas, NV. The Institutes CPCU Society’s annual meeting and CPCU conferment celebration is three days of peer-led education and designation recognition. It overlaps directly with TMPAA, so pick one. Go if you are conferring a CPCU, active in a CPCU chapter, or want technical education rather than market access. November 2026 November is genuinely quiet for commercial P&C. The fall circuit spends itself by late October and the industry turns to January 1 renewals. The one significant national event is on the life and benefits side. Protectors Vegas November 9 to 11, The Venetian, Las Vegas, NV. NAIFA and Connectiv have rebuilt NAIFA’s flagship conference as Protectors Vegas, positioned as the largest gathering of the life and annuity industry. It convenes more than 1,500 advisors, carriers, distributors, technology providers, and investors across three streams: distribution, product and strategy, and technology and innovation. NAIFA has offered a complimentary all-access pass to qualified client-facing agents, advisors, and agency principals. Go if your agency has a life, annuity, or benefits practice. If you are pure commercial P&C, use November to catch up on the renewals you ignored in October. How to actually get value out of a conference Most brokers come home from a big show with a tote bag and no decisions. A few habits change that. Book meetings before you land. At ILF, WSIA, and TMPAA the entire value is the pre-scheduled calendar, and walking the floor cold wastes a flight. Bring real documents to technology shows. Carry the carrier PDF that always breaks, the agency template with the unusual tables, and the renewal that took your team a full day. Ask vendors to run them live, at the booth. Ask what the price actually includes. Implementation fees, per-seat minimums, per-module add-ons, and annual lock-in contracts are where a cheap-looking demo becomes an expensive system. Ask how fast support responds. Not whether they have support, but the actual response time when a live client deliverable breaks on a Friday afternoon. Pick one problem per show. Go in with a single bottleneck you want solved and evaluate everything against it. Where CopyCat will be in 2026 CopyCat will have a booth at both ends of the spectrum this fall: the regional show for the agencies doing the work, and the national show for the whole industry. Event Dates Where to find us ABU SoCal Mini-vention August 28 Trade show floor, 1:00 to 4:00 p.m., DoubleTree Ontario Airport ITC Vegas Sept 29 to Oct 1 Expo floor, Mandalay Bay Convention Center Bring a carrier quote to either booth and we will build the proposal in front of you: your template, your branding, with page-level citations back to the source document. That is the whole demo. It either works on your paperwork or it does not. What we will tell you at the booth, so you can skip the line On pricing, it is a flat monthly fee. No hidden charges, no implementation fee, no per-module add-ons that turn the useful parts into a growing invoice, and no annual lock-in. You can leave whenever. When new capabilities ship they are included at the same price rather than sold back to you as an upgrade. On support, you reach the actual team instead of a ticket queue. Several customers have told us replies come back within five minutes. Our formal commitment is to resolve product issues within six hours, and we hold to it during renewal season, which is the only time it matters. On reliability, every extracted value is traceable to the page it came from, so a producer can defend a number in front of a client. We do not train AI models on customer documents. Both founders sat for the commercial broker exam before building this, because a proposal is a coverage document, not a marketing asset. If you want to look before the show, see how CopyCat generates commercial insurance proposals , compares quotes with citations , or builds employee benefits workbooks .

title: AtriCure Announces that the First Patient has been Treated with the Revolutionary AtriClip® FLEX-Mini™ Device
summary: MASON, Ohio--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Aug. 27, 2024-- AtriCure, Inc. (Nasdaq: ATRC), a leading innovator in surgical treatments and therapies for atrial fibrillation (Afib), left atrial appendage (LAA) management, and post-operative pain management, today announced that the first patient was treated with the AtriClip® FLEX-Mini™ device, which recently received 510(k) clearance. The AtriClip FLEX-Mini sets a new standard as the smallest profile surgical LAA device on the market and builds upon the proven technology of AtriCure’s AtriClip platform, with ease of use and design simplicity that offers enhanced access and increased visibility for physicians. “The AtriClip FLEX-Mini is an unparalleled product that reinforces our position as the market leader in surgical LAA management,” said Michael Carrel, President and Chief Executive Officer at AtriCure. “With nearly 600,000 AtriClip devices sold globally, we are having a significant impact on patients’ lives. Continuing to innovate and enhance the unique features of our AtriClip platform will support even greater growth in this market.” The AtriClip FLEX-Mini, the smallest surgical LAA device available in the market, incorporates the trusted elements of the AtriClip portfolio, featuring a fully enclosed design with parallel beams for continuous closing force, ensuring optimal pressure on atrial tissue. The low-profile design enhances visibility without compromising stability, providing physicians with unprecedented control during procedures. Additionally, the device's ergonomic handle design enables single-handed placement, further simplifying the application process. “The AtriClip FLEX-Mini is a significant step forward in ensuring patients receive the best possible treatment,” said Dr. Ibrahim S. Sultan, MD, Professor and Chief, Division of Cardiac Surgery, University of Pittsburgh Medical Center. “This device builds off the first- and second-generation platforms, which established an incredible record of clinical outcomes. With surgical LAA management now having the highest-level recommendation for treatment from multiple physician societies, this new technology will make it even easier for my surgeon colleagues to choose mechanical appendage closure.” For more information about the AtriClip line of products, visit our website at www.atricure.com/laa-exclusion Forward-Looking Statements This press release contains “forward-looking statements”– that is, statements related to future events that by their nature address matters that are uncertain. We assume no obligation to update any forward-looking statements contained in this release and the related attachment as a result of new information or future events or developments, except as may be required by law. About AtriCure AtriCure, Inc. provides innovative technologies for the treatment of Afib and related conditions. Afib affects more than 37 million people worldwide. Electrophysiologists, cardiothoracic and thoracic surgeons around the globe use AtriCure technologies for the treatment of Afib, reduction of Afib related complications and post-operative pain management. AtriCure’s Isolator® Synergy™ Ablation System is the first medical device to receive FDA approval for the treatment of persistent Afib. AtriCure’s AtriClip® Left Atrial Appendage Exclusion System products are the most widely sold LAA management devices worldwide. AtriCure’s Hybrid AF™ Therapy is a minimally invasive procedure that provides a lasting solution for long-standing persistent Afib patients. AtriCure’s cryoICE cryoSPHERE® probes are cleared for temporary ablation of peripheral nerves to block pain, providing pain relief in cardiac and thoracic procedures. title: What is ERC-4337?
summary: Stackup explains how EIP-4337 account abstraction enables smart contract wallets with social logins, gasless transactions, one click multi-operations, and more!
body_text: ‍ ERC-4337 is an Ethereum standard that enables Account Abstraction , allowing users to interact with the Ethereum network through smart contract wallets without needing to directly manage private keys or native ETH for gas fees. What are the components of ERC-4337? The ERC-4337 standard enables account abstraction by creating an alternative transaction pool (also called amempool) for account abstraction transactions. It has four main components: UserOperations, Bundlers, EntryPoint, and Contract Accounts. UserOperations are pseudo-transaction objects that are used to execute actions through a smart contract wallet. Bundlers package UserOperations and send them to the EntryPoint contract on the blockchain for verification and execution. EntryPoint is a singleton smart contract that handles the verification and execution logic for transactions. Contract Accounts are owned by a user and can be supplemented with features from other smart contracts like aggregators and paymasters. ‍ How ERC-4337 Enables Account Abstraction The alternative mempool, managed by Bundlers, gets past the restriction of most EVM blockchains that only an EOA (externally owned account with a private key) can initiate transactions. Here is the process is a diagram: How ERC-4337 Enables Account Abstraction First, a user creates a UserOperation object and submits it to the mempool. The Bundler then receives the UserOperation and submits it to the EntryPoint for verification and execution. The EntryPoint verifies the UserOperation is valid by checking the Contract Account and if needed the Paymaster and Aggregator, and then sends the call data to the Wallet Contract for execution. Any unused gas fees are refunded to the Wallet Contract or a function is called on the Paymaster Contract to run any post-execution logic. The ERC-4337 standard has the potential to revolutionize the way users interact with the Ethereum network and could make it easier for non-technical users to participate in the Ethereum ecosystem. However, it is important for all implementations of the ERC-4337 standard to be thoroughly audited to ensure security and reliability.

title: How to File a Duty Drawback Claim: A Step-by-Step Guide
summary: A step-by-step guide to filing a duty drawback claim with CBP: gathering import data, matching exports, the ABI Drawback module, CBP Forms 7551 and 7553, accelerated payment privileges, and typical timelines.
body_text: How do I file a duty drawback claim? + Duty drawback claims are filed electronically with CBP through the ABI (Automated Broker Interface) Drawback module. The process is: gather your duty-paid import data, match it to qualifying exports or destructions, prepare the drawback entry (CBP Form 7551), file any required Notice of Intent to Export/Destroy (CBP Form 7553), submit through ACE, and receive payment after CBP review. Most companies file through a licensed customs broker. What forms do I need to file duty drawback? + The core form is CBP Form 7551, the drawback entry, filed electronically through ABI. If you plan to claim on exported or destroyed goods, you may also need CBP Form 7553 (Notice of Intent to Export, Destroy, or Return Merchandise) submitted before the export or destruction. You'll also reference your import entry summaries (CBP Form 7501) and proof of export or destruction. Can I file a duty drawback claim myself? + Technically yes, but it's difficult. You'd need to establish an electronic connection to CBP's ABI system or use a certified service bureau, and the documentation and HTS-matching rules are unforgiving — a single error can disqualify a claim. In practice, nearly all drawback is filed by licensed customs brokers, and first-time filers are strongly advised to use one. What is accelerated payment in duty drawback? + Accelerated payment (AP) is a CBP privilege that lets approved claimants receive their drawback refund before CBP completes final review (liquidation) of the claim. It requires a bond. Without AP, you wait until the claim is fully liquidated, which can take considerably longer. First-time filers typically apply for AP and other privileges when they set up their drawback program. How long does it take to get a duty drawback refund? + With accelerated payment privilege, refunds can be paid within a few weeks to a couple of months of filing. Without accelerated payment, standard claims are paid after final liquidation, which can take 6-18 months. Timelines depend on claim complexity, documentation quality, and CBP's review queue. What documents do I need to file a drawback claim? + You need import entry summaries (CBP Form 7501) showing duties paid, HTS classifications, proof of export (bills of lading, AES export filings) or CBP-witnessed proof of destruction, and records tracing the duty-paid imports to the corresponding exports or destructions. For manufacturing claims you also need a bill of materials. Records must be retained for 3 years from the date the claim is liquidated. Do I need a customs broker to file duty drawback? + Practically, yes. Drawback documentation is detailed — chain of custody, HTS matching, export proofs — and errors disqualify claims. Licensed brokers experienced in drawback handle the ABI filing, privilege applications, and recordkeeping. Most ongoing drawback programs are run by brokers under contract with the importer.
